articles.titleCn: 习近平呼吁深化中埃合作，提出中东新安全架构建议

articles.summaryCn: 习近平在开罗与埃及总统塞西会谈，提出深化合作并倡导构建中东安全新架构，双方签署多项合作协议。

In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations. Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a {{1}} international and regional landscape. Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via {{6}} a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security. Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in fighting side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship.

Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience. Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better {{7}} their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as {{8}} development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and {{9}} new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, {{10}}, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology.

articles.title: Iran hits back after US launches new strikes
articles.titleCn: 美国发动新一轮打击后，伊朗进行反击
articles.summary: The latest US strikes against Iran and Iran's reported retaliation have further escalated tensions in and around the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington and Tehran trading accusations and threats of further military action.
articles.summaryCn: 美国对伊朗发动新打击后，伊朗革命卫队宣布报复性袭击美国基地，双方紧张局势升级，同时卡塔尔等国加紧外交斡旋。

paragraphs.en: Multiple {{0}} were heard on Tuesday evening across Iran's southern Hormozgan and southeastern Sistan and Baluchestan {{1}}, as US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the start of strikes against targets belonging to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Blasts were heard in the counties of Sirik, Bandar Abbas and Qeshm in Hormozgan, as well as Konarak and Chabahar in Sistan and Baluchestan, the semi-official Fars News Agency reported. 伊斯兰革命卫队周二晚间表示，已开始对地区内美国基地和资产发动打击，以报复美国的攻击。在其官方新闻机构塞帕新闻发表的一份声明中，伊斯兰革命卫队表示，其“针对侵略者的令人遗憾的回应”已经开始，并指出其防空部队击落了一架“敌对”的美国MQ-9“死神”无人机。其航空航天部队还对约旦的蒂廷营地和巴林的谢赫伊萨空军基地发动了弹道导弹和无人机打击，据称打死“大量”美军士兵，并摧毁了多个关键设施和武装直升机。声明强调，美国的打击只会延长霍尔木兹海峡的关闭时间，并使伊朗武装部队更加决心“镇压干涉该水道的 foreign 势力”。伊斯兰革命卫队表示，袭击是在美国“出于绝望”轰炸伊朗南部海岸多个民用地点之后开始的，也是对美国在霍尔木兹甘省对一场婚礼仪式发动的“罪恶”和致命袭击的报复。约旦武装部队-阿拉伯军随后表示，周二晚间，该国防空系统拦截并摧毁了伊朗过去数小时内进入该国领空的13枚弹道导弹中的10枚。

约旦武装部队声明称，另外三枚导弹落在远离人口中心的偏远地区，没有报告人员伤亡。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于2026年8月28日在得克萨斯州休斯顿的NASA林登·B·约翰逊航天中心与空间站机组人员通电话。特朗普警告将采取“更严厉”行动
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周二在Truth Social上发帖，称美军对伊朗的军事打击“规模大且威力强”，并警告称，如果伊朗进行报复，将面临更严厉的打击。特朗普在Truth Social上发帖警告称，如果伊朗“对这一非常正当的袭击进行报复，他们将再次遭到打击，力度和级别都会高得多。

特朗普在帖子中威胁称：“但这不会是最大的一次打击，更大规模的打击正在酝酿之中，一旦结束，伊朗伊斯兰共和国将所剩无几！”在接受福克斯新闻电话采访时，他声称美军摧毁了伊朗网络中的“大量雷达”，包括德黑兰试图重建的系统。特朗普说：“今天是一次非常大的打击。如果再有第三次，他们将作为一个国家被彻底消灭。”他补充说：“乔治·华盛顿号航母已满载弹药。”

“我们已经满载。”
据福克斯新闻报道，特朗普表示，在最新打击之前已通知海湾盟友。伊朗外交部发言人伊斯梅尔·巴加埃周二驳斥了美国的说法，称其“撒谎”，美国声称最近对伊朗拉拉克岛的袭击是因为伊朗军队准备在霍尔木兹海峡布雷。巴加埃在每周新闻发布会上指出，美国频繁声称伊朗有意发展核武器，称华盛顿的模式是“每次编造谎言为其罪行辩护”。

卡塔尔周二表示，正在加强与地区伙伴的外交努力，以迅速解决霍尔木兹海峡危机，并警告称，若问题得不到解决，将导致进一步升级。外交部发言人马吉德·安萨里在每周媒体简报会上表示，在最近几天的一系列外交访问和磋商之后，与包括阿曼和巴基斯坦在内的卡塔尔调解伙伴的讨论仍在进行中。安萨里表示，目前还没有可宣布的“实质性成果”，但未来几天将公布讨论和访问的进一步结果，并补充说，过去几天的外交努力主要集中在解决霍尔木兹海峡局势上。

他说，卡塔尔正在与合作伙伴合作，确保危机通过“保证海峡开放的外交解决方案”结束。安萨里补充说，这样的解决方案应允许该地区的产品进入全球市场，保障地区安全，并满足该地区人民对繁荣与安全的愿望。

articles.fullText:
On the morning of August 26, a massive mountain disaster struck the China-Nepal border. A glacier collapse in Nepal triggered an ice‑rock avalanche, which evolved into a devastating debris flow and flash flood.
A wall of ice, rock and debris plunged from the northern slope of Langtang Lirung in Nepal, roughly 5,200 meters above sea level. In a mere seven minutes, this destructive force travelled 22 kilometers through deep mountain gorges and slammed into Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, destroying roads, buildings and claiming lives on both sides.
The speed and scale of the disaster have raised difficult questions: Where did it actually begin? What made it so destructive? Could it have been predicted? And what can be done to reduce the risks before the next such event?
Where did the disaster begin?
According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), the catastrophic debris flow and flooding was likely triggered by rapid slope failure involving a glacier in Nepal's Langtang National Park, near the China-Nepal border. The USGS estimated that the resulting debris flow and flood travelled nearly 100 kilometers downstream.
Chinese geological experts reached a similar preliminary conclusion.
The Ministry of Natural Resources said analysis of high-resolution satellite imagery before and after the event, combined with seismic data and images from the disaster area, showed that the source was in Nepal, in the upper reaches of the Cuojian River, a tributary upstream of the Gyirong Port area.
The Xizang regional government further verified and mapped out the complete disaster propagation path: a glacier on the northern slope of Langtang Lirung fractured at an altitude of around 5,200 meters, descended to roughly 4,000 meters, and then travelled about 22 kilometers along the river channel before reaching Gyirong Port.
Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology has also received preliminary information indicating that an ice avalanche on the Nepali side may have temporarily dammed the Lhende River, forming a short-lived barrier lake before water surged downstream.
How ice rock collapse turned into a mudslide, and why the disaster was so destructive
The answer lies partly in the region's extreme terrain.
The collapse initiated at roughly 5,200 meters above sea level, dropped to around 4,000 meters, and continued down a steep valley for more than 20 kilometers toward terrain sitting at about 1,800 meters elevation.
That enormous vertical drop endowed the initial mass failure event with tremendous kinetic energy.
Chinese experts with the Ministry of Natural Resources estimate the debris flow moved at an average speed exceeding of 50 meters per second – over 180 kilometers per hour.
Its destructive power grew progressively as it advanced.
Ice and rock from the source zone scoured loose moraine, soil, water and boulders off the riverbed. What began as a relatively localized high-altitude collapse thus evolved into a far larger debris flow system.
Why was it so difficult to predict?
This may be the hardest question.
Weather forecasts can flag heavy rainfall. Water level sensors can detect rising river stages. Satellite imagery can capture changes in glaciers and mountain slopes.
Yet predicting the exact moment a high-altitude glacier or ice rock mass will collapse remains extremely challenging.
The core challenge stems from the harsh conditions of glacial source zones. According to Fan Xuanmei, director of the National Key Laboratory of Geohazard Prevention and Geoenvironment Protection at Chengdu University of Technology, these high elevation zones feature rugged, inaccessible terrain and severe climatic conditions, making installation and sustained maintenance of monitoring equipment enormously difficult.
While the Xizang Autonomous Region has completed a comprehensive inventory of more than 50,000 glaciers – systematically documenting their locations, coverage, surface areas and ice reserves – full predictive capacity is still out of reach. Scientists cannot yet precisely forecast collapse timing, failure magnitude, and subsequent evolution into high speed debris flows for every unstable glacier or ice rock slope.
Zhang Qianggong, head of the Climate and Environmental Risk Unit at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), further explains that existing monitoring frameworks are built mainly for glacial lake outburst floods and lack coverage for direct glacier and ice rock collapses. Remote, jagged topography severely constrains sensor deployment, and there are currently no cost-effective, universally applicable technical solutions for full-scale glacial early warning.
Fan Xuanmei notes that her team is developing an integrated "space air ground" monitoring and intelligent early-warning system. Such a system could buy extra lead time, granting downstream communities precious minutes to evacuate, close roads and safeguard rescue personnel.
Rescue, facts and cross border cooperation
The latest official casualty tally released by Xizang authorities stood at 16 dead and 546 missing, based on figures recorded at 6 p.m. on August 29. Authorities also reported 261 missing foreign nationals from 23 countries, and said relevant foreign embassies and consulates had been notified.

As of September 1, rescuers were still conducting intensive searches across the core disaster zone while restoring access roads and communications and monitoring secondary hazards.
China's Foreign Ministry says it has shared disaster zone imagery, satellite and hydrological data with Nepal, including early warnings concerning an upstream barrier lake. It adds that China has delivered emergency and humanitarian assistance, with an initial 50 tonnes of relief supplies arriving in Kathmandu.
China is rolling out a package of assistance to Nepal, including emergency cash grants and humanitarian aid, in the wake of this severe cross-border disaster triggered by glacial collapse, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Saturday.
Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said the two sides have maintained smooth communication on search and rescue operations, information sharing and secondary disaster prevention.
"We have been providing Nepal with meteorological and hydrological data, conducted expert consultations, and shared early-warning information," Guo said. "China will continue giving strong support to Nepal in its relief efforts and strengthen cooperation on disaster prevention and control for the shared benefit of both peoples."

8月26日上午，一场大规模山地灾害袭击了中尼边境。尼泊尔境内的一次冰川崩塌引发了冰岩崩，演变成毁灭性的泥石流和山洪。一堵由冰、岩石和碎屑组成的墙从尼泊尔朗塘利隆峰北坡（海拔约5200米）倾泻而下。短短七分钟内，这股破坏力穿越深山峡谷奔袭22公里，冲击了中国西南部西藏自治区的吉隆口岸，摧毁了道路和建筑，并在两国造成人员伤亡。灾害的速度和规模引发了难题：它究竟从哪里开始？

是什么让它如此具有破坏性？能否提前预测？在下一次此类事件发生前，又能做些什么来降低风险？灾害从哪里开始？根据美国地质调查局（USGS）的说法，这场灾难性的泥石流和洪水很可能是由尼泊尔朗塘国家公园内（靠近中尼边境）一处冰川的快速坡体失稳所触发。

USGS估计，由此产生的泥石流和洪水向下游奔流了近100公里。中国地质专家得出了类似的初步结论。自然资源部表示，对事件前后高分辨率卫星影像的分析，结合地震数据和灾区图像，显示源头位于尼泊尔境内，即吉隆口岸上游的措坚河上游。西藏自治区政府进一步核实并绘制了完整的灾害传播路径：朗塘利隆峰北坡的一处冰川在海拔约5200米处断裂，下降到约4000米，然后沿河道行进约22公里到达吉隆口岸。尼泊尔水文气象部也已收到初步信息，表明尼泊尔一侧的冰崩可能暂时堵塞了林德河，形成了一个短暂的堰塞湖，随后水流向下游涌去。

冰岩崩如何演变成泥石流，以及为何灾害如此具有破坏性。答案部分在于该地区极端的地形。崩塌在海拔约5200米处开始，下降到约4000米，并沿着陡峭的山谷继续向下延伸20多公里，到达海拔约1800米的地带。巨大的垂直落差赋予了初始块体失稳事件巨大的动能。中国自然资源部专家估计，泥石流的平均速度超过每秒50米——超过每小时180公里。其破坏力在推进过程中不断增强。

来自源区的冰和岩石冲刷了河床上的松散冰碛、土壤、水和巨石。最初相对局部的海拔崩塌因此演变成一个规模大得多的泥石流系统。为什么如此难以预测？这可能是最难回答的问题。天气预报可以预警强降雨。

水位传感器可以检测河流水位上升。卫星图像可以捕捉冰川和山坡的变化。然而，预测高海拔冰川或冰岩体崩塌的确切时刻仍然极具挑战性。核心挑战源于冰川源区的恶劣条件。据成都理工大学地质灾害防治与地质环境保护国家重点实验室主任范宣梅介绍，这些高海拔地区地形崎岖、难以进入，气候条件恶劣，使得监测设备的安装和持续维护极其困难。

虽然西藏自治区已完成对5万多条冰川的全面清查——系统记录了它们的位置、覆盖范围、面积和冰储量——但全面的预测能力仍遥不可及。科学家目前还无法精确预测每个不稳定冰川或冰岩坡的崩塌时间、失稳规模以及随后演变为高速泥石流的过程。国际山地综合发展中心（ICIMOD）气候与环境风险部门负责人张强弓进一步解释说，现有的监测框架主要针对冰湖溃决洪水，缺乏对直接冰川和冰岩崩塌的覆盖。偏远崎岖的地形严重限制了传感器的部署，目前还没有成本效益高、普遍适用的全规模冰川预警技术解决方案。范宣梅指出，她的团队正在开发一个集成的“空天地”监测和智能预警系统。

这样的系统可以争取额外的预警时间，为下游社区提供宝贵的分钟来疏散、封闭道路并保护救援人员。救援、事实与跨境合作。西藏当局公布的最新官方伤亡统计为16人死亡，546人失踪，数据截至8月29日下午6时。当局还报告了来自23个国家的261名外国公民失踪，并表示已通知相关外国使领馆。随着搜索队找到遗体、核实身份并交叉核对失踪人员报告，这些数字仍可能发生变化。

截至9月1日，救援人员仍在核心灾区进行密集搜索，同时恢复通道和通讯，并监测次生灾害。中国外交部表示，已与尼泊尔分享了灾区图像、卫星和水文数据，包括有关上游堰塞湖的预警。外交部补充说，中国已提供紧急和人道主义援助，首批50吨救援物资已抵达加德满都。外交部长王毅周六表示，在这场由冰川崩塌引发的严重跨境灾害之后，中国正在向尼泊尔提供一揽子援助，包括紧急现金赠款和人道主义援助。中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆表示，双方在搜救行动、信息共享和次生灾害预防方面保持了顺畅沟通。

“我们一直在向尼泊尔提供气象和水文数据，进行专家磋商，并分享预警信息，”郭说。“中国将继续大力支持尼泊尔的救援工作，并加强防灾减灾合作，造福两国人民。”

articles.fullText:
An aerial view of the Central Business District in Egypt's New Administrative Capital, east of Cairo, Egypt. /Embassy of China in Egypt
China and Egypt are celebrating the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year, with bilateral ties deepening across an increasingly broad range of areas. Trade and investment remain important pillars, while cooperation is gaining momentum in digital technology, green energy and cultural exchanges.
Egypt was the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with China. The two countries upgraded their relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership in late 2014, and bilateral ties have deepened across multiple fields under the Belt and Road Initiative.
As a key project under China-Egypt Belt and Road cooperation, the Central Business District in Egypt's New Administrative Capital, east of Cairo, was built by a Chinese company. The project includes a 385.8-meter skyscraper, which is set to become the tallest building in Africa.
The 70-year relationship is increasingly reflected not only in the volume of goods traded between the two countries, but also in the industries being developed, technologies being introduced and exchanges taking place on the ground.
Zero tariffs open the Chinese market to more Egyptian goods
Official data shows that China has been Egypt's largest trading partner for 14 consecutive years, with bilateral trade reaching a record $20.79 billion in 2025. Egypt's imports from China are concentrated in engineering equipment, textiles and building materials, while its exports to China are mainly agricultural and food products.
Five products – frozen strawberries, beet pulp, raw flax, natural pigments and natural calcium phosphate – accounted for 46.1% of Egypt's exports to China.
The trade figures have strengthened further this year. Since May 1, China has applied zero tariffs to products from 53 African countries that have diplomatic relations with China, including Egypt.
Egypt's exports to China rose 199.8% year on year to $840.8 million in the first half of 2026, up from $280.5 million in the same period last year, according to Egypt's Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).
The policy is also changing how some Egyptian companies approach the Chinese market.
At an "Export to China" event in Cairo on August 17, Chinese and Egyptian companies signed trade agreements worth nearly $170 million. More than 10 Chinese companies, including CITIC Group, China General Technology Group and Poly Group, held talks with Egyptian businesses.
Ma Guanghui, executive vice president of the Egyptian Chinese General Chamber of Commerce Association, said Egyptian businesses are paying greater attention to Chinese market requirements.
A flax factory with a total investment of $58 million in Sadat City, which produces about 3,800 tonnes of flax yarn a year, previously supplied only the European Union market. It is now pursuing Oeko-Tex certification and preparing to enter China's high-end home-textile market, with its profit margin expected to increase by 8 to 10 percentage points, Ma said.
Egyptian farmers harvest flax in Sharqia, Egypt, on April 14, 2025. 
Chinese investment expands Egypt's industrial capacity
As global supply chains shift and trade protectionism rises, Egypt's position at the crossroads of Africa, Asia and Europe is taking on new significance. For Chinese companies, investment in Egypt is creating opportunities to expand manufacturing while contributing to the country's industrial development and connecting both sides to broader regional markets.
The China-Egypt TEDA Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone began construction in 2008. By the end of June 2026, more than 200 companies had established operations in the zone, attracting over $4.7 billion in investment and generating more than $7.3 billion in cumulative sales, Cao Hui, executive director of Egypt-TEDA Special Economic Zone Development Co., said.
Its development has helped strengthen Egypt's industrial base, with Chinese companies becoming increasingly integrated into the local economy. Jushi Egypt, a subsidiary of China Jushi, began operations in the zone in 2012 and now runs Africa's largest fiberglass production base.
By the end of 2025, Chinese companies had invested more than $1.5 billion in Egypt's photovoltaic industry. Elite Solar opened a 5GW solar manufacturing complex in Egypt early this year.
As Egypt's industrial base expands into higher-value sectors, China-Egypt cooperation is also moving into emerging technology sectors.
In Sohag, a city in southern Egypt, the China-Egypt Belt and Road Joint Laboratory for Renewable Energy has produced Egypt's first locally manufactured high-efficiency half-cell solar module, helping strengthen the country's capabilities in photovoltaic technology and local manufacturing.
Digital infrastructure is another area of growing cooperation. An Egyptian government data and cloud computing center using Chinese technology was completed in April 2024, and Egypt's first public cloud node began operating the following month. More than 200 companies now use the platform.
A technician inspects solar modules at the China-Egypt Belt and Road Joint Laboratory on Renewable Energy in Sohag, Egypt. /Embassy of China in Egypt
Exchanges deepen between two ancient civilizations
The relationship also extends into education and archaeology. Chinese is now part of Egypt's national education system, with 30 universities offering Chinese departments or courses and more than 20 secondary schools offering Chinese as an elective.
In 2018, Chinese and Egyptian researchers launched a joint archaeological project at the Temple of Montu in Luxor, bringing the two countries together to study one of the world's oldest civilizations and share expertise in archaeology.

五种产品——冷冻草莓、甜菜粕、生亚麻、天然色素和天然磷酸钙——占埃及对中国出口的46.1%。今年贸易数据进一步加强。自5月1日起，中国对包括埃及在内的53个与中国有外交关系的非洲国家产品实行零关税。根据埃及中央公共动员和统计局（CAPMAS）的数据，2026年上半年，埃及对中国的出口同比增长199.8%，达到8.408亿美元，而去年同期为2.805亿美元。这项政策也在改变一些埃及公司进入中国市场的方式。

在8月17日于开罗举行的“出口到中国”活动中，中埃公司签署了价值近1.7亿美元的贸易协议。包括中信集团、中国通用技术集团和保利集团在内的10多家中国公司与埃及企业举行了会谈。埃及中国总商会执行副会长马广辉表示，埃及企业越来越重视中国市场的需求。位于萨达特城的一家亚麻工厂总投资5800万美元，年产约3800吨亚麻纱，此前仅供应欧盟市场。马广辉说，该工厂现在正在申请Oeko-Tex认证，准备进入中国高端家纺市场，其利润率预计将提高8至10个百分点。

2025年4月14日，埃及农民在埃及沙尔基亚收获亚麻。中国投资扩大埃及的工业产能。随着全球供应链转移和贸易保护主义抬头，埃及地处非洲、亚洲和欧洲十字路口的地位正呈现出新的重要性。对中国公司而言，在埃及投资正在创造扩大制造业的机会，同时有助于该国的工业发展，并将双方与更广泛的区域市场联系起来。中埃泰达苏伊士经贸合作区于2008年开始建设。中非泰达苏伊士经济特区发展有限公司执行董事曹慧表示，截至2026年6月底，已有200多家公司在合作区开展业务，吸引投资超过47亿美元，累计销售额超过73亿美元。

其发展帮助加强了埃及的工业基础，中国公司越来越融入当地经济。中国巨石子公司巨石埃及于2012年在合作区开始运营，现拥有非洲最大的玻璃纤维生产基地。截至2025年底，中国公司在埃及光伏产业的投资超过15亿美元。今年早些时候，Elite Solar在埃及开设了一个5GW的太阳能制造综合体。随着埃及的工业基础向更高价值的领域扩展，中埃合作也正在进入新兴技术领域。

在埃及南部城市索哈杰，中埃“一带一路”可再生能源联合实验室生产了埃及首块本地制造的高效半片太阳能组件，有助于增强该国在光伏技术和本地制造方面的能力。数字基础设施是另一个日益增长的合作领域。一个使用中国技术的埃及政府数据和云计算中心于2024年4月完工，埃及首个公有云节点于次月开始运营。目前有200多家公司使用该平台。一名技术人员在埃及索哈杰的中埃“一带一路”可再生能源联合实验室检查太阳能组件。

两大文明古国交流深化。这种关系还延伸到教育和考古领域。汉语现已成为埃及国民教育体系的一部分，有30所大学开设中文系或中文课程，20多所中学将中文作为选修课。2018年，中埃研究人员在卢克索的蒙图神庙启动了一个联合考古项目，将两国聚集在一起，研究世界上最古老的文明之一，并分享考古专业知识。

articles.fullText:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035.
The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other transformative technologies: data, AI, genomics and wearables.
Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an immersive 3D headset and a video-game-like console.
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of specialties including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery.
Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The precision of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take strain off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge bottlenecks.
"The ability to have lots of integrated computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of complications like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery.
Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to undergo lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this groundbreaking title, but the news "didn't faze" the 76-year-old retired detective.
Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet. "It was extraordinary," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." He had undergone non-robotic keyhole surgery for a different cancer in the past, and says the recovery time was "much longer". This time, he was driving his wife to the garden centrer for coffee less than a week later.
Stamenkovic runs fellowships at St Bartholomew's training surgeons on this new technology. He says it is the young surgeons who pick up the new robotic control system the fastest and who become the most adept.
"They've come with different skill sets," he says, "they've probably come with gaming skill sets, some of them have come with a musical background."
Laying out his long-term mission, Stamenkovic added: "All we need to do is harness their energy, their passion, their skill set, and teach them the right moves. And that will make the surgeon of the future."
articles.fullTextCn:
英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年，英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院，外科医生和护士使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是首批接受培训使用美国公司Initiative制造的新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统的人员。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机器人手臂，通过沉浸式3D头戴设备和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

此类机器人手术系统可用于多种专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸外科或普外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，高级心胸外科培训生Ali Ansaripour（右）在机器人专科培训中观摩。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

机器人辅助手术的精准性应能缩短住院时间并加快恢复，这将缓解目前面临漫长等待名单、劳动力短缺和出院瓶颈的医疗服务的压力。“在人类控制的机器人技术之上集成大量计算机辅助技术的能力，使这种手术精准且安全，”巴茨健康NHS信托机器人手术与研究主任Sasha Stamenkovic说。

除了改善恢复时间，更高的精准性还降低了并发症风险，如肺手术后常见的导致住院时间延长的漏气问题。在圣巴塞洛缪医院，护士使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统协助肺癌手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

Ian Macleod是英国NHS中首位使用新型达芬奇机器人系统进行肺癌手术的患者。Macleod说，直到穿上手术服并被麻醉时，他才意识到自己将获得这一开创性称号，但这一消息“没有吓到”这位76岁的退休侦探。机器人辅助手术后30分钟，Macleod就能重新站立。

“这太不可思议了，”他说，“事实上，手术后我很快发现只有一针缝合。”他过去曾因另一种癌症接受过非机器人微创手术，并表示那次恢复时间“长得多”。而这次，不到一周后他就开车带妻子去花园中心喝咖啡。Stamenkovic在圣巴塞洛缪医院举办专科培训，教授外科医生这项新技术。他说，年轻外科医生掌握新机器人控制系统最快，也最熟练。

“他们带来了不同的技能，”他说，“可能带有游戏技能，有些人有音乐背景。”Stamenkovic阐述其长期使命时说：“我们只需利用他们的精力、热情和技能，教他们正确的动作。这将造就未来的外科医生。”
